problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ b & c\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}\,$ is given above. What is the value of $b+c?$
worked_solution:
Since the matrix of the quadratic form must be symmetric, we rewrite our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =1{x}_{1}^{2}+(-3){x}_{1}{x}_{2} \\  & +\,(-3){x}_{2}{x}_{1}+1{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that to get a symmetric matrix, we must split the coefficient of $-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$ between the entries 

$$
{a}_{12}={a}_{21}=\frac{-6}{2}=-3
$$

of our matrix. So, the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $b=-3$ and $c=1.$ Finally, 

$$
b+c=-3+1=-2.
$$
